summary: Foundations for child chats, behind the staged flag hub_children (HUB_CHILDREN_ENABLED in src/shared/hub.ts, false; SB_HUB_CHILDREN=1 or the backend setting labs.hub_children turns it on). Any chat can become a parent; there is no chat type and no column on conversations. This change adds the tables hub_parents, hub_batches, hub_children and hub_wakes (a wake holds a summary and a pointer into the child's transcript, never a report body), their CRUD with every conversation id resolved to its root, the hub.* settings with defaults and ranges (no UI yet), and the pure rules childState, parentState, grantedMode, hubNeedsCard (a card only in plan and supervised modes), runSlotFree, wakeBatchDecision, the pointer parser and the brief and update wrappers, with shared fixtures. Nothing reads the flag outside tests, so no behaviour changes. The migration time is logged through the db.migrate perf span. Starting children (PR 5): with the flag on, every chat that is not an open child gets the MCP tools start_children and list_children and a short hub paragraph in its MCP instructions. start_children (1 to 8 tasks) opens one approval card in plan and supervised modes (plan mode itself is refused) and starts at once in auto-accept edits and above, with a stored row that lists the children. The same plan twice returns the open card. A child gets min(requested, parent) as its mode, its own worktree (purpose hub-child, branch namespace hub) or the project folder, and every node_modules folder of the project cloned before its first turn, which is the brief wrapped in <switchboard-hub-brief>. The batch is refused when free disk after it would fall under hub.minFreeGiB (5 GiB). At most hub.runningPerInstance (3) children per account and hub.runningPerParent (6) per parent run a turn at once; the others wait for a slot. One failed child becomes failed_start with a failed wake, and the batch goes on; a child cut off by a quit gets the same at the next start. The backend refuses a user turn to an open child (code child_read_only, on SUBMIT_USER_TURN and SEND_TURN, so every client and transport), and a peer message to it from anyone but its parent. A child gets no parent tools. Measured: perf spans hub.batch, hub.start-child (worktree, clone and launch times, disk use), hub.child-turn (tokens, cost, duration per child turn) and hub.resources (every 30 s while children are open: RSS, CPU % and process count of each child's and parent's agent process tree, the app's main heap, renderer CPU and total RSS).

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/hub-rules.test.ts tests/unit/hub-db.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: childState, parentState, grantedMode, hubNeedsCard, runSlotFree and wakeBatchDecision pass every case in tests/fixtures/hub-cases.json; the flag helper is off by default and on with SB_HUB_CHILDREN=1 or labs.hub_children; readHubSettings keeps in-range values and falls back to defaults; hub_parents, hub_batches, hub_children and hub_wakes CRUD, the open-child lookup by child_id, wake delivery once per wake, and a rotated Claude id resolving to its root conversation.
A copy of a real 1.1 GB desktop database migrated with this build (five new tables, no other change), and the migrate code of origin/main then opened the migrated file.

npx vitest run tests/unit/hub-start.test.ts tests/unit/provider-registry-hub.test.ts tests/unit/hub-measure.test.ts tests/unit/dependency-clone.test.ts tests/unit/worktree-creation-contract.test.ts tests/unit/switchboard-mcp-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: one card per batch in ask mode and the same plan again returns it; full access starts 3 children on two providers with no card and a mode no higher than the parent; plan mode, a child as a parent and a batch the disk cannot take are refused; 4 children on one account run 3 and the 4th starts when a turn ends; one failed child leaves the others started with one failed wake; a quit mid-start marks the child failed; a user turn to an open child is refused on SUBMIT_USER_TURN and SEND_TURN; a child gets no parent tools and no hub paragraph; the bridge reports its agent's pid; the dependency scan finds node_modules up to 3 levels.
